chunks: Ibn Abi al-Bilad narrated from his father, from one of his companions, who attributed it to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), that he said to one of his companions:

How will you be when the two examiners of the grave come to you? He said, 'O Messenger of Allah, what are the examiners of the grave?' He said, 'Two angels, harsh and severe, with voices like rumbling thunder and eyes like blinding lightning. They will tread on their own hair and plough the ground with their fangs, and they will question you.' He asked, 'And you will be in a state such as this?' He replied, 'You will be as you are in your present state.' He said, 'Then I will be able to face them.'

key_terms.فَتَنَا الْقَبْر: The examiners of the grave (Munkar and Nakir)

ai.seo_question: Who are the two examiners of the grave and what is their role in Shia eschatology?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Kitab al-Zuhd* vividly depicts the terrifying physical attributes of the angels Munkar and Nakir, whose voices resemble thunder and eyes flash like lightning, emphasizing the gravity of the *Barzakh* (intermediate state). The Prophet’s reassurance to his companion highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis that one's spiritual preparedness and adherence to faith during life are the primary defenses against the trials of the grave.

en.shaykh-tahir-ridha-jaffer: 8.Ibn Abī al-Bilād narrated from his father, from one of his companions who attributed it to the Prophet (ṣ), that he said to one of his companions, “How will you be when the two examiners of the grave come to you?”

So he (the companion) asked, “O Messenger of Allah, what are the examiners of the grave?” He said, “Two angels, harsh and severe, with voices like rumbling thunder and eyes like blinding lightning. They will be treading on their own hair and ploughing the ground with their [large] fangs; they will [come to] question you.” He asked, “[Will that be] when I am in a state such as this?” He replied, “[Yes,] you will be as you are in your present state.” He said, “Then I will be able to face them.”’”
